[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) with Angular"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial outlines how to set up a CI/CD pipeline for an Angular application. CI/CD automates the build, test, and deployment processes, ensuring faster and more reliable releases."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic understanding of Angular development."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A Git repository (e.g., GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A CI/CD platform account (e.g., Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, CircleCI)."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Node.js and npm installed locally."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Setting up the Angular Project"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a new Angular project (if you don't have one already):"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"ng new my-angular-app
cd my-angular-app"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Initialize a Git repository and commit your initial code:"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit""},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Configuring CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions Example)"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a `.github/workflows` directory in your project root."},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a YAML file (e.g., `ci-cd.yml`) inside the `.github/workflows` directory to define your CI/CD pipeline."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"name: Angular CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '16.x'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Build
        run: ng build --configuration production

      - name: Run tests
        run: ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadlessCI
"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Commit and push the workflow file to your Git repository."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Understanding the CI/CD Workflow"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"The workflow is triggered on `push` events to the `main` branch and on `pull_request` events targeting the `main` branch."},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"The workflow runs on an `ubuntu-latest` runner."},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"The workflow performs the following steps:"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Checks out the code using `actions/checkout@v3`."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Sets up Node.js using `actions/setup-node@v3`."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Installs dependencies using `npm install`."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Builds the Angular application using `ng build --configuration production`."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Runs unit tests using `ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadlessCI`."},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Adding Deployment (Example: Firebase Hosting)"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, install the Firebase CLI globally:"},{"order":29,"type":"code","text":"npm install -g firebase-tools"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Log in to Firebase:"},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"firebase login"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"Update the `ci-cd.yml` file to include deployment steps:"},{"order":33,"type":"code","text":"name: Angular CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '16.x'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Build
        run: ng build --configuration production

      - name: Run tests
        run: ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadlessCI

      - name: Deploy to Firebase Hosting
        uses: w9jds/firebase-action@releases/v6
        with:
          args: deploy --only hosting
        env:
          FIREBASE_TOKEN: '${{ secrets.FIREBASE_TOKEN }}'
          PROJECT_PATH: dist/<your-app-name>"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace `<your-app-name>` with the name of your Angular application (usually found in `angular.json` under `projects.<your-app-name>.architect.build.options.outputPath`)."},{"order":35,"type":"paragraph","text":"Add the `FIREBASE_TOKEN` secret to your GitHub repository settings (Settings -> Secrets -> Actions).  You can generate this token by running `firebase login:ci`."},{"order":36,"type":"paragraph","text":"Commit and push the updated workflow file."},{"order":37,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Other CI/CD Platforms"},{"order":38,"type":"paragraph","text":"The general principles remain the same for other CI/CD platforms like Jenkins, GitLab CI, and CircleCI. You'll need to adapt the configuration files to the specific syntax and features of each platform."},{"order":39,"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, GitLab CI uses `.gitlab-ci.yml`, and Jenkins uses a `Jenkinsfile` or a web-based configuration."},{"order":40,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a basic introduction to setting up a CI/CD pipeline for an Angular application. You can customize the workflow to fit your specific needs, such as adding more sophisticated testing, code analysis, or deployment strategies. Remember to always secure your deployment credentials and follow best practices for CI/CD."}]
